reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling NVA4 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, but the more useful figure is that only 25 of Virginia's 330 mapped data centers publish any power specification at all.

Sterling is a mid-tier facility within the disclosed set. Its 11 MW ranks 22nd of the 25 Virginia sites with published capacity, or 0.7 percent of the state total. The campus carries 128,715 square feet of technical space and no listed certifications. Its suitability score of 57 is derived from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion named as the missing input.

For AI specifically, 11 MW is a small building. Training campuses that anchor frontier model runs are measured in hundreds of megawatts, so this facility is not where compute scaling is decided. The disclosure gap matters more than the facility. When 305 of 330 mapped Virginia locations publish no power figure, any state-level estimate of available AI compute is a floor rather than a total, and the undisclosed remainder could be larger or smaller than what is visible.

The data does not say who leases the space, what accelerators run inside it, how much of the 11 MW is actually drawn, or how the site is fed and interconnected. It also does not cover expansion. Sterling's individual contribution to AI compute scaling is minor, and the state's real capacity is largely unmeasured.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
